text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Polish economy's performance is satisfactory, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) senior representative Markus Rodlauer said. The rate of the country's economic growth should be faster and exceed seven percent, World Bank representative Paul Knotter said.

- An experimental GSM digital mobile phone network will be operated in the northeastern Suwalki province to check the effects of the new telecom system introduction in areas of low conventional telecommunications infrastructure.
- Thursday's talks on the planned lay-offs of 352 workers between the management of the Sandomierz-based Pilkington Sandoglass glassworks and the trade unions ended in a fiasco.
- The listed Stomil Olsztyn tyre maker has modernised its second electrofilter in the plant's energy section. The filter's operational efficiency is now 99.4 percent.
- The Kruszwica fats and oils maker, to be listed next year, has corrected its annual profit forecast for 1996 down to 5.4 million zlotys.
- The Krakow-based Mostostal Krakow construction firm wants to enter 9.32 million shares for continuous trading on the Warsaw bourse.

- The National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank will sell a 21 percent stake in the Bank Rozwoju Budownictwa Budbank housing development bank in near future and invite bidders to the privatisation of the Pierwszy Komercyjny Bank (PKB) commercial bank, the NBP's deputy president Witold Kozinski said.
NOWA EUROPA

- A political contract between Solidarity trade union and the Polish Peasant Party (PSL) may lead to crediting the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard by the state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank, the oppositon centrist Union for Freedom (UW) chairman Leszek Balcerowicz said. The BGZ bank president Kazimierz Olesiak denied any knowledge of the scheme.
- The Szczecin Parnica shipyard will carry on building trawlers contracted by the family groups of Scottish fishermen, Parnica said.

- A telecom optical fibre cable-laying project currently under way to connect Poland and the Danish Bornholm island will be completed in a week's time, the Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) telekom monopolist Szczecin province branch director Zdzislaw Wojcik said.
- The private Netia Telekom SA has already invested $100 million in Poland's telecommunications development and will invest $600 million more by 2000, Netia's president Jan Guz said.
- The Gliwice-based Opel car factory will start its workers' search in March or April next year, General Motors-Poland director Scott Mackie said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Tyre maker Stomil Sanok wants to enter 1.55 million A-series shares for continuous trading on the Warsaw bourse.

- The Gdansk administrative court has ruled that Dutch Makro Cash and Carry wholesaler cannot build its trading centre in the Zaspa district because previous plans envisaged setting up a sports centre in the area.
- Poland's hotels and travel offices will be linked by a computer reservation system by the second half of 1997, the national sports and tourism agency deputy president Jan Blonski said.
ZYCIE

- The listed Rolimpex food processor and trader will participate in the privatisation of several sugar mills to strengthen its position in the oils and fats industry next year, Rolimpex president Roman Mlyniec said.

- The Polski Handel Spozywczy (PHS) foodstuffs wholesaler will reduce employment and sell most of its warehouses and nonprofitable shops in the restructuring operation currently under way, the PHS deputy president Miroslaw Bielicki said.
PARKIET
- "If you want to invest your money and go abroad for 15 years invest it in Poland - our favourite choice", the London-based Foreign & Colonial's chief analist Arnab Banerij said.
- Creditanstalt (CA) Securities will issue short-term commercial papers of CA Leasing Polska leasing firm.
- The state-owned BGZ bank and the British Know-How Fund will carry out a financial corporate restructuring programme (FCRP) worth 13 million pounds, BGZ said.
